{{Quote|It's a cold, hard galaxy we live in.|The Gand bounty hunter Zuckuss|<ref name="HM">''[[Hard Merchandise]]''</ref>}}
'''The galaxy''' was one of the billions of [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxies]] that existed in the [[Universe/Legends|universe]]. Composed of some four hundred billion [[Star/Legends|stars]] in a disk 120,000 [[light-year]]s in diameter, the galaxy was orbited by seven smaller satellite galaxies, of which five were directly accessible by the time of the Galactic Empire.<ref name="Intergalactic Passport real-life artifact">[[Intergalactic Passport (real-life artifact)|Intergalactic Passport]]</ref> The galaxy was home to between five and twenty million [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]], and over one hundred quadrillion sentient beings<ref name="TEA" /> lived in one billion [[Star system/Legends|star systems]], interacting with each other through travel, diplomacy, [[Galactic economy|trade]], [[Politics/Legends|politics]], and [[Space warfare/Legends|war]]. In historical memory, this galaxy had been ruled by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], and the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]], the [[Fel Empire]], [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]] and was home to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]-using orders of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]].

==Astrography==
===Structure===
{{Quote|A finite mind cannot comprehend the infinite galaxy.|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Abyss">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Abyss]]''</ref>}}
The galaxy was between 100,000 and 120,000 [[Light-year/Legends|light-years]] across, or 37,000 [[Parsec/Legends|parsecs]] (a parsec is 3.258 light years), and approximately 13 billion [[Standard year/Legends|years]] old. The galaxy's luminous disk contained some four hundred billion [[Star/Legends|stars]], of which around a quarter had been properly surveyed by the [[galactic community]] by the time of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The luminous disk revolved around the [[Galactic Center]], a [[Black hole/Legends|supermassive black hole]] that massed as much as four million suns. As late as the [[Declaration of a New Order]], only [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droids]] had ever visited the black hole at Galactic Center.<ref name="TEAIntro" /> The known galaxy included nearly a billion inhabited [[Star system/Legends|star systems]], from uncharted [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]]' settlements to planet-spanning [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|ecumenopoleis]] where scarcely a meter of ground remained untouched. Under the Galactic Empire, nearly seventy million of those system were sufficiently populated to merit some form of representation.<ref name="TEA" />

The galaxy bulged around Galactic Center to form a bright sphere known as the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]]. This region was around seven thousand light-years across and contained some thirty billion tightly-compacted stars. Towards the center the stars of the Deep Core were only around a hundredth of a light-year apart, and were known to collide and rip out each other's stellar cores. Most of the stars of the luminous galaxy were in a disk of spiral arms rotating around the Deep Core. Galactic civilization named four spiral arms: the [[Bakchou arm|Bakchou Arm]],<ref name="CampaignPack">''[[Star Wars Campaign Pack]]''</ref> the [[Ettarue arm|Ettarue Arm]],<ref name="Encyclopedia">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> the [[South Arm]],<ref name="SofS">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref> and the [[Tingel Arm/Legends|Tingel Arm]].<ref name="Star's End">''[[Han Solo at Stars' End]]''</ref> The brightest [[supergiant]] stars were concentrated in the spiral arms, as well as glowing clouds of gas and dust, which contributed to the apparent gaps between the arms even though those areas were full of stars.<ref name="TEAIntro" />

Most stars were within a thousand light-years above or below the plane of the luminous disk, forming a two thousand-light-year region known as the "thin disk". For three thousand, five hundred light-years on either side was the "thick disk", which was poorer in stars than the thin disk and even fewer of these had a system of [[Planet/Legends|planets]].<ref name="TEAIntro" />

===Stellar halo===
[[File:Galaxy1.png|thumb|right|250px|A portion of the galaxy, seen from above the galactic plane, showing the luminous disk, the spiral arms, and the bulge of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]].]]
Beyond the thick disk was the stellar halo, a huge sphere surrounding the entire galaxy with a few billion stars in highly elliptical orbits.<ref name="TEAIntro" /> Nearly two hundred globular clusters orbited in this region. The globular clusters were typically lifeless, packing hundreds of thousands of extremely old, inhospitable stars into only a hundred light-years. Many of the globular clusters, however, were considered extremely beautiful sights, such as [[Cosm's Well/Legends|Cosm's Well]].<ref name="TEA" />

The galaxy was orbited by seven dwarf satellite galaxies, some of which contained twenty billion stars. They were ranked in order of distance. The closest was Companion Aurek, also known as the [[Rishi Maze/Legends|Rishi Maze]], a complex tangle of stars high above the galactic plane. Companion Besh, also known as [[Firefist]], was some 150,000 light-years away from the galaxy and had only ever been surveyed by probots. The other satellite galaxies, [[Companion Cresh|Companions Cresh]] through [[Companion Grek|Grek]], were much further out. Most of the Companions were described as having ancient, metal-poor remnants of [[Star/Legends|stars]] and not much life.<ref name="TEA" />

A [[circumferential hyperspace barrier]] severely complicated [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] travel outside the disk and generally discouraged [[Extragalactic/Legends|extra-galactic]] exploration. A band of whorls and eddies that spun around the galaxy too quickly to be traversed at faster-than-light speeds, a number of [[Astrophysicist/Legends|astrophysicists]] believed this to be a creation of a mysterious ancient race known as the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]].<ref name="Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut &mdash; The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref> Beyond the galaxy's rim, separating it from other galaxies, was a vast expanse of starless space known as the [[Intergalactic Void]].<ref name="Star Wars 1977 38">[[Star Wars (1977) 38|''Star Wars'' (1977) 38]]</ref><ref name="The New Jedi Order: The Final Prophecy">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Final Prophecy]]''</ref>

===Stars===
While there was a hyperspace disturbance outside of the galaxy, hyperspace made it possible ''within'' the galaxy to have an enormous and diverse civilization. Of the galaxy's 400 billion stars, around 180 billion of them were orbited by a [[Star system/Legends|system]] of planets. 90% of the stars of the galaxy fell within the Main Sequence (the other 10% comprised [[Protostar/Legends|protostars]] or stellar remnants like [[White dwarf/Legends|white dwarfs]], [[Neutron star/Legends|neutron stars]] and [[Black hole/Legends|black holes]]). The larger blue and white stars of the sequence - the O-, B-, and A-type stars - such as [[Garnib (star)/Legends|Garnib]], [[Kessa/Legends|Kessa]] and [[Colu/Legends|Colu]], lived for a few million years and rarely possessed systems that had intelligent life since it had too little time to evolve. The most habitable stars were G- and K-type yellow and orange dwarfs such as [[Corell/Legends|Corell]] and [[Yavin/Legends|Yavin]], which had lifespans of tens of billions of years giving life plenty of time to evolve. G- and K-types between them made up 19% of the galaxy's stars, and 75% of them were habitable. The most common stars in the galaxy, however, were M-type [[Red dwarf/Legends|red dwarfs]], which comprised 70% of the galaxy's stars, but only 1% of them, such as [[Barab (star)/Legends|Barab]], were habitable. Very few red dwarfs were settled: most were surveyed by probe droids in the early years of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and were typically left abandoned unless they possessed mineable resources.<ref name="TEAIntro" />

Factoring in the output of heat and light needed for an advanced civilization to form, therefore, there were 7.1 billion truly habitable stars within the galaxy, and about 3.2 billion habitable star systems.<ref name="TEAIntro" /><ref name="TEA" /> It was estimated that about one billion of those systems were actually populated or had been settled by [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings.<ref name="TEAIntro" /><ref name="TEA" /><ref name="AtlasEndnotes" />

===Regions===
{{Quote|I've flown from one end of this galaxy to the other, and I've seen a lot of strange stuff.|Han Solo|<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
[[File:NJO_galaxy_map.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Stylized map of the galaxy, showing the various regions.]]
The galaxy had many regions, which were largely cultural entities as opposed to political ones, and generally corresponded to stages of galactic exploration and settlement. The nine most famous regions were the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]], the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]], the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]], the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]], the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]], the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], and beyond the galactic frontier, the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] and [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] and<ref name="TEA" /> Casual phraseology usually split the galaxy into "the Core" and "the Rim", with the latter consisting of the Expansion Region and parts beyond.<ref name="TEA" />

====Deep Core====
At the very heart of the galaxy, the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] (also known as the Core Systems) was a region that spanned seven thousand [[Light-year/Legends|light-years]], and contained roughly 30 billion stars. Due to the gravitational pull of the vast number of stars, as well as a massive [[Black hole/Legends|black hole]] at [[Galactic Center|the center]], local space-time was severely warped, making hyperspace travel difficult at best. For millennia, only the fringes of the Deep Core closest to the Core Worlds, within a mathematically defined boundary known as the [[Horizon]], had been settled. These worlds included [[Khomm/Legends|Khomm]], [[Thoadeye system/Legends|Thoadeye]], [[Vulpter/Legends|Vulpter]], and the dominant planet of the Deep Core, [[Empress Teta/Legends|Empress Teta]]. The heart of the region was thought to be almost inaccessible until [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] found several safe [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] into the region. The area remained fiercely loyal to the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], and was an Imperial stronghold until almost twenty years after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].<ref name="TEA" />

====Core Worlds====
The [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] was an ancient region bordering the outlying areas of the Deep Core, and included some of the most prestigious, well-developed, well-known, and heavily populated planets in the galaxy. The Galactic Republic and subsequently all galaxywide governments were born in the Core Worlds and spread out over the galaxy. During both the time of the Republic and Empire, Coruscant, a major core world, was the Galactic [[Capital/Legends|Capital]]. The region of the Core Worlds known as the [[Tetrahedron]] became the cradle of the early Republic, and simultaneously scouts discovered the Perlemian Trade Route and the Corellian Run emanating from Coruscant, creating a region known as the [[Arrowhead]] containing the ancient worlds of [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]], [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]], [[Basilisk]] and [[Ixtlar/Legends|Ixtlar]]. Colonization created a semi-circular ring extending south as far as [[Abregado-rae/Legends|Abregado-rae]], often considered the cream of the Core Worlds, while subsequent centuries create a second ring to the galactic west, though these worlds, disparaged as "[[the Negs]]" for their negative-digit [[Galactic coordinates/Legends|galactic coordinates]], were looked down upon by the rest of the Core. The Core's natural wealth was buoyed by the farming worlds of the [[Agricultural Circuit]], the semi-independent colonies of the [[Illodia sector/Legends|Illodia sector]], the [[Bormea/Darpa Corridor]], the manufacturing planets of the [[Humbarine sector/Legends|Humbarine sector]], and the military [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]] of the [[Kuat sector/Legends|Kuat sector]].<ref name="TEA" />

====Colonies====
The [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]], so named because it was among the first areas outside the Core to be colonized, contained many of the galaxy's wealthiest worlds and prided itself on being the galaxy's economic engine. Worlds here were typically heavily populated, industrialized, and cultured, and the region was considered the meeting point of Core wealth and Rim raw materials. The Colonies, forming the tip of [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]], came to include many of the galaxy's oldest manufacturing worlds, including [[Balmorra/Legends|Balmorra]], [[Commenor/Legends|Commenor]] and [[Neimoidia/Legends|Neimoidia]]. Subsequent colonization produced the shipyards of [[Loronar/Legends|Loronar]], the urbanized worlds of the [[Pencael system/Legends|Pencael system]], and the young worlds of [[Yabol Opa/Legends|Yabol Opa]] with its great university, the [[Fortress world/Legends|fortress world]] of [[Raithal/Legends|Raithal]], and the farm worlds of the [[Delle system/Legends|Delle system]].<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:JKA_galaxy.png|thumb|left|250px|A schematic view of the galaxy.]]

====Inner Rim====
The [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] was a region of the galaxy between the Colonies and the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]]. It was originally just called "The Rim", as it was expected to be the farthest extent of the known galaxy for [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]], but the Expanded Rim (later renamed the Expansion Region) was opened within a hundred years of the Inner Rim being settled during the [[Great Manifest Period/Legends|Great Manifest Period]]. Inner Rimmers tended to see themselves as being part of the Core and looked disdainfully upon the "outer galaxy", but were known to resent and envy the greater wealth and history of the Core Worlds. The region had minimal cultural influence and had few truly notable planets beyond the ecumenopolis of [[Denon/Legends|Denon]] and the medical worlds of [[Manaan/Legends|Manaan]] and [[Thyferra/Legends|Thyferra]]. As the bridge between the Core and the Rim, the Inner Rim held great strategic value, and during both the Clone Wars and the Galactic Civil War, brutal battles were fought over the region.<ref name="TEA" />

====Expansion Region====
The [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]] began as an experiment in corporate-controlled worlds, known as the [[Exploitation Region]], with powerful corporations exploiting and profiting heavily from the planets for their raw materials, metals and [[Ore/Legends|ores]]. Inhabitants were oppressed while the corporations stripped entire stellar systems along the Corellian Run of all their resources. The damage was so catastrophic that colonization shifted spinward to the Perlemian Trade Route, which was responsible for the conspicuous northern "bulge" of the modern Inner Rim's border. Colonization resumed during the Great Manifest Period, but the [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|Alsakan Conflicts]] destroyed many of the Expansion Region's worlds in [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]], shifting colonization west of the Corellian Run, creating a stretch of space known as the [[77 Sectors]] that was dominated by Corellians for millennia. This part of the Expansion Region thrived, with the Rimma, Hydia, and Corellian Trade Spine Routes opening up the region and linking worlds like [[Tynna/Legends|Tynna]], the [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] homeworld of [[Kinyen/Legends|Kinyen]], and trading planets of the [[Harrin Trade Corridor]]. This region's citizens often preferred to think of themselves as being apart from the rest of the luckless Expansion Region, which continued to suffer during the Republic's final millennium. A second, disastrous experiment in corporate control known as the [[Outer Expansion Zone/Legends|Outer Expansion Zone]] ravaged the region and the [[Outer Expansion Zone scandal|resulting scandal]] forced the Senate to disband the [[Expansionist Oligarchy/Legends|Expansionist Oligarchy]], but the final centuries of the Republic saw the Slice sectors of the Region fall into economic ruin. The story was told by the region's trade routes: while the Core, Colonies and Inner Rim were dense webs of tangled [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]], the Expansion Region was ill-served by routes and the casual observer might think that it had never been settled. Expansion Region worlds continued to be producers of raw materials and ores. However, most natural resources were exhausted by the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]], with [[Gyndine/Legends|Gyndine]], [[Bacrana/Legends|Bacrana]] and [[Cyrillia/Legends|Cyrillia]] being among the few remaining viable ports.<ref name="TEA" />

====Mid Rim====
With fewer natural resources (and therefore a smaller population) than many neighboring regions, the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] was a territory where residents worked hard for everything they had. Colonization began as the Expansion Region was settled, and while corporations continued to prefer to exploit that region, homesteading incentives and development grants from Coruscant were instead picked up by religious communes or local political confederations. The Slice in the Mid Rim was colonized slowly over several millennia, following a crosshatching pattern determined by Coruscant, giving rise to an orderly region whose residents had plenty of room to spread out. Corporate exploitation remained in the Expansion Region while lawlessness gravitated to the less-governed [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], which were opened for colonization at the same time. Consequently, the Mid Rim built up a successful economy based on low-cost manufacturing and agriculture, and following the blazing of the Hydian War in [[3693 BBY]], the northern and southern arcs of the Mid Rim came into shape. Historic Republic outposts like [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]] or lost colonies like [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] found themselves at the heart of new, orderly, government zoned settlement districts, some of which retained their alphanumeric identifications for centuries. Few of the Mid Rim's worlds became famous, but among those that did were the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] homeworld of [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] and the [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] homeworld of [[Iridonia/Legends|Iridonia]], the ocean planet of [[Glee Anselm/Legends|Glee Anselm]], the [[Order of the Sacred Circle]]'s retreat of [[Monastery/Legends|Monastery]], and [[Ansion/Legends|Ansion]], the nexus of several hyperlanes linked by the [[Keitumite Mutual Military Treaty]].<ref name="TEA" />

====Outer Rim Territories====
The [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] was the largest region of the galaxy, and the last widely settled expanse before [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] and the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]. It was strewn with obscure worlds, and rugged, primitive frontier planets. Due to its distance from the Core, government control was historically the weakest in the Outer Rim Territories, and it was the traditional refuge for dissidents, pilgrims and freedom-seekers, but it was also beset by lawlessness, oppression and violence. The worlds of the Outer Rim were immensely varied as a consequence: [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]] was a prosperous, industrialised megalopolis, and [[Entralla/Legends|Entralla]] was a vibrant, [[High Human Culture/Legends|Human-dominated]] spaceport world, but [[Terminus/Legends|Terminus]] and [[Aduba-3/Legends|Aduba-3]] were criminal-run [[Shadowport/Legends|shadowports]], and [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] was a Hutt-controlled trade depot. The Outer Rim was also dotted with barely-habited worlds like [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]], [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], [[Tund/Legends|Tund]] and [[Muskree]]. Worlds closest to the major [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|super-hyperroutes]] tended to be the most civilized, but far from these trade links, they tended to be dominated by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]]. Mass settlement of large portions of the Outer Rim did not begin until after [[5500 BBY/Legends|5500 BBY]], when colonists took advantage of the new trade routes of the Hydian, the Rimma, and the Corellian Trade Spine. Settlement in the southern quadrant was rapid, but expansion in the northern quadrant was hampered by the [[Great Galactic War]] and the horrors of the [[Kanz Disorders/Legends|Kanz Disorders]]. In a reversal of the galaxy's usual pattern, colonization was slowest in the Slice, dominated as it was [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]]. Republic authority in the region all-but collapsed during the [[New Sith Wars]], and arguably never returned, with the Hutts filling the power vacuum and piracy, slavery and anarchy dominating. In [[124 BBY]], the Senate declared the whole region a [[Free Trade Zone/Legends|Free Trade Zone]] in an effort to jump-start economic development, but this was exploited by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], and the Senate re-imposing taxation in [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]] was the trigger for the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] and the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]]. The Galactic Empire oppressed much of the Outer Rim, leading to greater sympathy for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] in the region, but the New Republic and the Galactic Alliance both failed to impose central control in the area, leaving the Outer Rim much as it had been for centuries.<ref name="TEA" />

====Unknown Regions====
[[File:FateOutboundFlight-TEA.png|thumb|right|250px|Part of the Unknown Regions, showing the of the [[Chiss Ascendancy/Legends|Chiss Ascendancy]] and the planned route of the ''Outbound Flight'' .]]
The term "[[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]" referred to those areas that had not been directly surveyed by Republic or Imperial scouts. It was most commonly applied to the less-known parts of the galaxy's western disk, a quadrant stretching roughly between [[Bakura/Legends|Bakura]] and the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]]. However, the term also applied to the galaxy's halo of gas, dust and stars, as well as the satellite galaxies. When the aggregate of all this territory is summed, the Unknown Regions reached nearly triple the size of settled space, but by some calculations, just 15% of the galactic disk's total stellar mass qualified as part of the Unknown Regions. The chunk of the Unknown Regions within the galaxy was a product of the lack of any western analogues to the Perlemian Trade Route and the Corellian Run, and the Republic's early scouts were content to expand into the easier-to-reach territories of [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]]. It later became clear that the route to the west was in fact barred by a [[Western barrier|tangle]] of hyperspace disturbances that effectively split the galaxy in half, forming the midline of the [[Circumferential hyperspace barrier|galactic barrier]] that enveloped the galaxy. The barrier to the Unknown Regions was permeable, however, with [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] tales telling of strange ships visiting distant Outer Rim ports like Terminus, hyperdrive mishaps taking ships through the divide, or ancient alien trails allowing access to the region.<ref name="TEA" />

The ill-fated [[Outbound Flight Project]] was one of the first official attempts to penetrate the Unknown Regions, while the Galactic Empire's [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] spent several years mapping portions of the area. The [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] were the dominant species of the Unknown Regions, but in comparison to known space, where most amoral or expansionist species were cowed or exterminated by the early Republic, the Unknown Regions were still a savage, anarchic area. Other powerful species within the region included the [[Vagaari Empire|slaver empire]] of the [[Vagaari/Legends|Vagaari]], the illusion-spinning mollusks called [[Croke]]s, the religiously-fanatical [[Ssi-ruu]]k, and the [[blind berserker]]s of the [[Leech Legion]]. Outside the disk, in the satellite galaxy of [[Firefist|Companion Besh]], lived the [[Nagai/Legends|Nagai]] and their oppressors, the [[Tof/Legends|Tofs]]. The Nagai invaded known space in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], pursued by the Tofs, and joined forces with the [[Alliance of Free Planets]] to defeat their oppressors and returned to Firefist to liberate it.<ref name="TEA" />

Normalization of relations with the [[Chiss Ascendancy/Legends|Chiss Ascendancy]] after the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] led to the establishment of stable hyperroutes into the Unknown Regions through the [[Utegetu Nebula/Legends|Utegetu Nebula]], such as the [[Rago Run]], and by [[44 ABY]] the name was largely inaccurate, at least when applied to the galactic disk. The galactic halo and the satellite galaxies, however, remained poorly explored and mysterious.<ref name="TEA" />

====Wild Space====
[[File:Wildspace1.jpg|thumb|left|200px|By 0 BBY, Wild Space often referred to the southeast of the galactic disk.]]
[[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] was the frontier of galactic society and was not a formal label, but was applied to the unsettled galactic fringe and other parts of the galaxy with negligible colonization or development. Wild Space by the Imperial Period typically referred to the wispy fringe of the galaxy's eastern disk, as well as the narrow, meandering strip that separated the civilized galaxy from the Unknown Regions. One of Emperor Palpatine's last acts was to open up much of the region to more extensive exploration. Wild Space differed from the Unknown Regions in that some of Wild Space had been explored, though not extensively, and the findings recorded in official logs; the Unknown Regions remained mysterious. The worlds of Wild Space largely ignored the central government, and were generally peaceful, but many acted as criminal hideaways.<ref name="TEA" />

====Other terms====
[[File:Miscellaneous_regions.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Map showing the galaxy's main regions, miscellaneous smaller territories, and client states and [[Allied Region]]s.]]
The galaxy's nine main regions did not reflect the full reality of its political and cultural divisions. Within the territorial bands between the Core and the Outer Rim lay a number of groupings and prefectures, some that had their own regional governments, and others that had only shared cultural stereotypes. The largest of these was [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]], a vast region of space between the Perlemian and the Corellian Run generally considered the center of galactic civilization and commerce. At its tip was the [[Arrowhead]], encompassing the Core Worlds part of the Slice, with Coruscant at its point. The Arrowhead's other two vertices traditionally fell on [[Vento system/Legends|Vento]] on the Perlemian and on Corellia itself, on the Run. The Arrowhead contained the elite of the Core Worlds, and grew out of the ancient [[Pre-Republic era|pre-Republic]] [[Tetrahedron]] that was the cradle of galactic civilization. Sometimes called the Inner Core, the Arrowhead included [[Ixtlar/Legends|Ixtlar]], [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]], [[Grizmallt/Legends|Grizmallt]] and [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]], which became ever-more prestigious the closer they were to Coruscant.<ref name="TEA" />

Colonists out of the Arrowhead settled the Slice, going out into what became known as the Colonies, and then further beyond. The worlds along the Perlemian and the Corellian Run were settled for millennia, and colonization slowly reached out from both to knit the Slice together. The Core, Colonies and Inner Rim portions of the Slice were thickly-settled and crisscrossed with thousands of hyperlanes and [[praedium]]s; the Expansion Region was heavily-colonized near the Corellian Run (and dominated by Corellian interests), but more sparsely settled south of the Perlemian, the product of the millennia-long [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|Alsakan Conflicts]]. The Slice's luster had begun to fade by the time colonists pushed beyond the Expansion Region in the central Slice; the Mid Rim reaches were well-surveyed but thinly-settled, and the Hutts dominated the Outer Rim precincts even beyond Hutt Space. Though new industries and businesses had largely moved beyond the Slice by the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the region was still considered the heart of galactic civilization, a distinction its citizens remained proud of.<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Southern Core]] was settled from the Arrowhead and grew through contact with a number of advanced ancient civilizations, including the [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronians]], the [[Herglic/Legends|Herglics]], and the [[Atrisian Commonwealth/Legends|Atrisian Commonwealth]]. This made it a polyglot region that resisted easy characterization. The western quadrant of the Core Worlds long resisted exploration, lacking any [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|super-hyperroutes]] and limiting progress along hyperlanes like the [[Metellos Trade Route/Legends|Metellos Trade Route]] to one- or two-light-year hops. Worlds settled along this western frontier received a negative first digit in their [[Galactic coordinates/Legends|galactic coordinates]] owing to their position west of Coruscant, earning them the name "[[the Negs]]," dooming such areas as the [[Farlax sector/Legends|Farlax sector]] to perennial second-class status within the Core.<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Northern Dependencies/Legends|Northern Dependencies]], a long-settled region north of Coruscant, generally looked outward, whether to [[Nouane (Allied Region)|Nouane]], the worlds of the Hydian Way, or the [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]] beyond. Some of the galaxy's greatest traders, explorers and entrepreneurs hailed from the Northern Dependencies, and the region included some of the galaxy's eldest worlds, rarely troubling itself with Core World politics. To its northeast, the region north of the Perlemian Trade Route, was the [[Trans-Hydian/Legends|Trans-Hydian]], an area dotted with worlds with ancient histories, such as [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] or the planets of the [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith Worlds]] and the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]], but largely sidelined economically until late in galactic history. Economic development jumped from the Slice to the [[Trailing Sectors/Legends|Trailing Sectors]] further south, and then followed the Hydian Way into the New Territories. For millennia, the threat of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]], rumors of the ancient Sith, and geographic oddities such as the vast [[Radama Void/Legends|Radama Void]] encouraged more profitable enterprises elsewhere. The Trans-Hydian owed its name to traders from [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]] and [[Celanon/Legends|Celanon]], who braved the threat of Mandalorian raiders to blaze new trade routes like the [[Listehol Run/Legends|Listehol Run]], the [[Shaltin Tunnels/Legends|Shaltin Tunnels]] and the [[Gordian Reach/Legends|Gordian Reach]] to link the Hydian and the Perlemian. After the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the region's loyalties were split between the Empire and the New Republic across the area known as the [[Trans-Hydian/Legends|Trans-Hydian]].<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Trailing Sectors/Legends|Trailing Sectors]] were settled during the [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|Alsakan Conflicts]], which saw many colonies in the Slice ruined, enslaved or depopulated, pushing colonization west of the Corellian Run. Here, intrepid traders had long done business with the Herglics, [[Givin/Legends|Givin]] and [[Tynnan/Legends|Tynnans]], and the Expansion Region's Trailing Sectors soon outstripped the Slice sectors, jumpstarting expansion into the Mid Rim. The rise of the Rimma Trade Route in [[5500 BBY/Legends|5500 BBY]] and the Hydian Way two thousand years later furthered this long boom, knitting the region together for traders from across the galaxy. Denizens of the Trailing Sectors tended to view their region as having built on the successes and traditions of the Slice while disregarding its mistakes, valuing entrepreneurship and and hard work.<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Western Reaches/Legends|Western Reaches]] grew up around the Corellian Trade Spine and the Hydian Way, with settlement flowing in from the Southern Core and the Trailing Sectors and inheriting those regions' diversity and sense of independence. Explorers and settlers continued to expand the region as late as the period of the New Republic, pushing further west into the Unknown Regions. The Reaches' independence and distance from Coruscant historically made them a hotbed of rebellion, being the refuge for the [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|last holdouts]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] after the Clone Wars. The Galactic Empire launched a [[Western Reaches Operation|massive campaign]] to pacify the Western Reaches, but the area remained a refuge for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] throughout the Galactic Civil War and was the site of many Imperial atrocities.<ref name="TEA" />

The [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]] were beyond the Northern Dependencies in a region that had developed slowly in contrast to much of the galaxy. Worlds such as [[Ithor/Legends|Ithor]], Ord Mantell and Iridonia were well known, but they were isolated outposts. Large-scale efforts to promote settlement in the northern quadrant repeatedly failed, leading to disasters like the [[Kanz Disorders/Legends|Kanz Disorders]] and the [[Outer Expansion Zone/Legends|Outer Expansion Zone]]. The region was finally properly settled in the final years of the Republic, with the [[D'Asta family|D'Asta merchant family]] of [[Serenno/Legends|Serenno]] establishing markets along the [[Braxant Run/Legends|Braxant Run]] while the [[Nalroni Merchant Council]] expanded along the [[Celanon Spur/Legends|Celanon Spur]]. These economic successes encouraged Coruscant to invest heavily in the region, soon dubbed the New Territories, and between Republic spending on programs like the [[Planetary Pioneers]] and the influence of the D'Asta family, the region was strongly [[Loyalist/Legends|Loyalist]] during the Clone Wars and the Galactic Civil War. The New Territories was the core of many Imperial successor states after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], and it became the contested frontier between the New Republic and the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]]. The New Territories were devastated during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], and struggled to rebound afterwards.<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Galactic Rim/Legends|Galactic Rim]] was a term for the edge of the galaxy and was remote to most civilisation.<ref name="RP">''[[Rogue Planet]]''</ref> The Galactic Rim was slightly less luminous as the stars faded out.<ref name="EE1">[[Empire's End 1|''Empire's End'' 1]]</ref> However, the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] was fully aware that the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] had established a [[Praetorite Vong|foothold]] in the edge of the galaxy.<ref name="OF" /> With the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] having a vast [[Unidentified Imperial shipyard|shipyard]] there, that would then be used by the [[Dark Empire]].<ref name="EE1" />

==History==
===Formation===
{{Main|Timeline of galactic history/Legends}}
{{Quote|&hellip;there's very little in this universe that rises above the mean and petty. Maybe the stars themselves.|Princess Leia Organa|<ref name="Splinter">''[[Splinter of the Mind's Eye]]''</ref>}}
Some [[13,000,000,000 BBY|thirteen billion years]] before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], an immense cloud of gas and dust collapsed under its own gravity and coalesced to form a revolving disk, creating the galaxy.<ref name="EGtAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']], p. x.</ref> Over many more billions of years, the [[Star/Legends|stars]] and [[Planet/Legends|planets]] began to form. By [[5,000,000,000 BBY]], life had begun to evolve in the galaxy, with some of the earliest examples of non-sentient life developing on [[Goroth Prime/Legends|Goroth Prime]].<ref name="Goroth">''[[Goroth: Slave of the Empire]]''</ref>

Around [[2,000,000 BBY]], many of the galaxy's most well-known species were evolving: the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]] began on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] as a species of tree-climbers.<ref name="EGtAS" /> [[The Oracle (Pelgrin)|The Oracle]] of [[Pelgrin]], quite possibly the oldest artifact in the galaxy, was believed to date from this period.<ref name="POTJS">''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]''</ref> By [[200,000 BBY]], the [[Zhell/Legends|Zhell]], ancestors to the [[Human/Legends|Humans]], had developed intelligence and were waging [[Zhell–Taung war|war]] against the [[Taung/Legends|Taungs]] for control of their mutual [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Notron]], later known as [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="Author's Cut 2">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-2-ancient-coruscant|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 2 - Ancient Coruscant}}</ref>

===The earliest civilizations===
[[File:Rakatan_Empire_Atlas.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The galaxy under the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]].]]
By [[100,000 BBY/Legends|100,000 BBY]], a mysterious race known as the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]] dominated the galaxy. Also known as the Architects, this spectacularly powerful race was believed to have been capable of manipulating and moving the very stars: surviving Celestial machinery like [[Centerpoint Station]] and the [[Cosmic Turbine]] could manipulate gravity on a titanic scale with [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsor]] pulses, [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beams]], and [[Wormhole/Legends|hyperspace wormholes]]. With this technology, the Celestials were believed to have been responsible for building the [[Corellian system/Legends|Corellian system]], the [[Vultar system/Legends|Vultar system]], and 15 other star systems, as well as the [[Hapes Cluster/Legends|Hapes Cluster]], the [[Kathol Rift/Legends|Kathol Rift]], and [[Maw Cluster/Legends|the Maw]] black hole cluster.<ref name="TEA" /> Pre-Republic specialists believed the Celestials to also be responsible for the [[circumferential hyperspace barrier]], possibly as a defense against outside interference. They were also believed to be responsible for the [[Western barrier|chain]] of [[Hyperspace anomaly/Legends|hyperspace anomalies]] west of the Core that bisected the galaxy and prevented travel into the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]. Speculation holds that the Celestials had crafted the [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] anomalies that bisected the galaxy in order to contain the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

A number of other spacefaring races around this time became clients of the Celestials. The insectile [[Killik/Legends|Killiks]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] were exploited as laborers and were seeded across the galaxy, until around [[30,000 BBY]] when they [[Great Migration|disappeared]] into the west of the galaxy and into the Unknown Regions, presumably relocated by the Celestials. The [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]] and the [[Gree/Legends|Gree]] made use of structures known as the [[Infinity Gate]]s and [[hypergate]]s, respectively, to travel between planets and came into territorial conflict with each other. Other species fled to escape the Celestials: the [[Sharu/Legends|Sharu]] of the [[Rafa system/Legends|Rafa system]] far in the galactic east had a brief period of expansion, spreading their iconic plastic [[pyramid]] cities as far into the Core as [[Aargau/Legends|Aargau]], but this may have attracted the attention of the Celestials and the Sharu buried their cities and sought refuge in primitivism to escape them. Likewise, the [[Columi/Legends|Columi]] of [[Columus/Legends|Columus]] made surveys of both the Humans and the [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] in the Core and were unimpressed by what they found, but also fled back to their homeworld, perhaps to avoid retribution from the Celestials.<ref name="TEA" />

A [[Unidentified cosmic war|cosmic war]] was fought at one time in the galaxy's past.<ref name="marvel84">[[Star Wars (1977) 84|''Star Wars'' (1977) 84]]</ref> Around [[35,000 BBY]], the domain of the Celestials was usurped when the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] slave race [[Rakatan revolt|revolted]]. Stealing technology from the [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]], they waged [[War against Celestial client species|war]] against the other servant races,<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> and broke through the barrier surrounding the Unknown Regions into the galaxy proper and waged a war of extermination upon the Celestials. The eventual fate of the Celestials was unclear. They may have been trapped inside the galaxy by their barrier and destroyed by the Rakatan revolt, or they may have escaped through the barrier.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> By [[30,000 BBY]], the Celestials were nowhere to be found,<ref name="TUR">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref> and the Rakatan [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] had taken center stage.<ref name="TEA" />

The Rakata fanned out from their homeworld of [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]] in the [[Tempered Wastes]] of the Unknown Regions, using [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrives]] that channelled the power of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to guide them to worlds with strong Force signatures. The Infinite Empire occupied a scattering of systems across the galaxy, but vast tracts of territory between these holdings remained untouched, allowing smaller interstellar confederations to flourish. The [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronians]] and the [[Gossam/Legends|Gossam]] experimented with the [[Tumbledrive/Legends|tumble hyperdrive]], and while worlds like [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] and [[Duro/Legends|Duro]] were occupied by the Rakata, [[Human/Legends|Humans]], [[Duros/Legends|Duros]], [[Selonian/Legends|Selonians]] and [[Drall (planet)|Drall]] were able to study the principles of the [[Force-drive|Rakatan hyperdrive]]. The Rakata proved to be cruel masters, consigning entire subject populations to [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]]. After nearly five thousand years of dominance, the Rakatan Empire collapsed after a devastating plague swept through the Empire that stripped the Rakata of their ability to use the Force. A colonial slave revolt finished off the empire by [[25,200 BBY]].<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

===Galactic governance===
[[File:Atlas_pre-republic.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The post-[[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] galaxy, showing the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core]] around which the Republic was formed, the [[Hutt Empire]], and [[Xim's empire]].]]
The decline of the Infinite Empire coincided with the reverse-engineering and perfection of Rakatan [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] technology by the other species of the galaxy. Developing technological replacements to its Force-based components, various species struck out from their homeworlds, first with slower-than-light [[Sleeper ship/Legends|sleeper ship]] colonies, followed by the development of the [[hyperspace cannon]]. Through this re-use of Rakatan castoffs, a number of civilizations asserted themselves: the Humans and Duros dominated the Core, while the cetacean [[Herglic/Legends|Herglics]] built up their own [[Herglic Trade Empire|trade empire]] to the south. On the Rim, Human sleeper ship colonies formed the [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese civilization]], which was united into an [[Xim's empire|empire]] by [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot]], before coming into [[Xim Wars|conflict]] with the [[Hutt Empire|empire]] of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]].<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="NEC" />

This period coincided with the beginning of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] on [[Tython/Legends|Tython]] with its studies of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], as well as the religious rivalry between understandings of the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]] and [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark sides of the Force]]. [[Great Schism/Legends|Conflict]] between the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] would assert itself several times throughout galactic history, a cycle that continued beyond the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:GalacticExplorations.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A map of the progress of the exploration of the galaxy.]]
In [[25,000 BBY/Legends|25,000 BBY]], in the aftermath of the [[Unification Wars (Galactic Republic)|Unification Wars]], the various states of the Core assembled on Coruscant and signed the [[Galactic Constitution/Legends|Galactic Constitution]], establishing a civilization under a common law, language and currency, proclaiming the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. The Republic united the largely-Human [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], and the [[Core Founder/Legends|Core Founders]] included political players like Coruscant, [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]], [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], [[Duro/Legends|Duro]], [[Kuat/Legends|Kuat]] and [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], military strongholds like the [[Azure Imperium]] of [[Axum]] and [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]], as well as [[Esseles/Legends|Esseles]] and [[Rendili/Legends|Rendili]], emerging commercial hubs like [[Tepasi/Legends|Tepasi]], [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal IV]] and [[Humbarine/Legends|Humbarine]], and worlds important to the medical, diplomatic and philosophical arts, like [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]], [[Caamas/Legends|Caamas]], [[Rhinnal/Legends|Rhinnal]] and [[Shawken]].<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Expansionist Period/Legends|Expansionist Era]] coincided with the foundation of the Republic and saw the beginnings of the official charting and settlement of much of the galaxy's spiral. Scouts pushing east from Coruscant moved up two trade routes, the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]] and the [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]], which formed the boundaries of a vast wedge of space known as "[[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]]." At the end of the Corellian Run lay [[Kalarba/Legends|Kalarba]], a trade hub maintained by the merchants of [[Paqwepori]], while the Perlemian led to the trade worlds of [[Tirahnn/Legends|Tirahnn]], [[Nouane/Legends|Nouane]], and [[Roche asteroid field|Roche]].<ref name="EGW" /> No similar corridors were found to the galactic west, which resulted in much of that quadrant of the galaxy remaining unexplored and mysterious, becoming known as the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]. This expansion saw the Republic come into [[Tionese War|conflict]] with the Human civilizations of the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]]. After its victory in [[24,000 BBY]], the Republic swelled with more territory than it could initially govern as many systems clamored for protection against the depredations of the Hutts.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="NEC" />

[[File:Alsakan_Conflicts_map.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The galaxy from the [[Indecta Era]] to the [[Kymoodon Era]].]]
The [[Great Manifest Period/Legends|Great Manifest Period]] began in [[20,000 BBY/Legends|20,000 BBY]] with the widespread settling of the Slice, with the dense web of systems at its tip becoming known as the [[Arrowhead]]. This region became heavily-dominated by Coruscant while [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] dominated settlement around the Corellian Run. Rivalry between Coruscant and [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]] over policy on the Perlemian sparked the [[First Alsakan Conflict]] in [[17,000 BBY]], the start of the [[Indecta Era]], and though peace would be brokered between the two, the [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|Alsakan Conflicts]] would continue in an abbreviated form for some 14,000 years. The first five Alsakan Conflicts also discouraged settlement along the Perlemian, pushing colonists to the [[Corellian Hegemony]] in the [[Trailing Sectors/Legends|Trailing Sectors]] along the Corellian Run and the growing [[Corellian Trade Spine/Legends|Corellian Trade Spine]].<ref name="EGW" /><ref name="NEC" />

The [[Kymoodon Era]], opening in [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]], ushered another colonization boom on par with the Great Manifest Period. Improvements in the hyperdrive allowed many odd pockets of colonization to spring up in the unexplored northern and southern quadrants, and the Herglics joined the Republic, beginning a surge in development around the [[Hidakai Pool]], which would become the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]]. However, the era stored up the seeds for future conflict, as the Republic's borders increasingly abutted those of [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]], leaving isolated colonies open to raids by Hutt [[Slaver/Legends|slavers]]. Widespread resentment of the Hutts on the Rim was tapped by [[Contispex I/Legends|Contispex I]] and the [[Humanocentrism|Humanocentric]] [[Pius Dea]] religious sect to begin a series of [[Pius Dea Crusades|Crusades]] against the Hutts in [[12,000 BBY/Legends|12,000 BBY]]. The millennia-long [[Pius Dea Era]] would see many non-Human species conquered, persecuted, or exterminated until the [[Contispex dynasty]] was [[Seventh Alsakan Conflict|overthrown]] by the Jedi Order, and would foment extreme resentment among the species of the Rim. The subsequent [[Ductavis Era]] and [[Rianitus Period]] from [[11,000 BBY|11,000]]-[[8000 BBY]] would be periods of retrenchment and rebuilding following the Crusades.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="NEC" />

[[File:Pius_Dea_Crusades.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The galaxy during the [[Pius Dea Era]].]]
The [[Subterra Period]] of 8000-[[7000 BBY]] saw new mapping of the galactic southern quadrant, with colonies such as [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]] serving as anchors for the tangles of [[praedium]]s that linked the region. Scouts also penetrated the [[Rishi Maze/Legends|Rishi Maze]] around this time. However, the lack of a [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|super-hyperroute]] into the southern quadrant and the new colonies' general inaccessibility promoted lawlessness in the Rim and limited Coruscant's authority, which was believed to have contributed to the [[Second Great Schism]] of the Jedi Order in [[7003 BBY]], beginning a galaxy-wide uprising of [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] known as the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]]. In the war's aftermath, the defeated Dark Jedi were exiled beyond the Rim into the unexplored space north of the Perlemian. There, the [[Exiles]] settled the worlds of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] and [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]] within the [[Stygian Caldera]], where they dominated the native [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] and established an [[Sith Empire/Legends|empire]].<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="NEC" />

During the [[Manderon Period]], the [[Corellian Trade Spine/Legends|Corellian Trade Spine]] and the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]] were established in [[5500 BBY/Legends|5500 BBY]] after the Herglics, [[Givin/Legends|Givin]] and [[Corellian/Legends|Corellians]] linked together hundreds of pre-existing praediums, improving access to the southern quadrant. In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], the Sith Empire was rediscovered by the Republic, beginning the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] when the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] attempted to conquer the Republic. The [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] were defeated and once again driven into exile, but it was the beginning of a threat that would trouble the Republic for the remainder of its existence. A thousand years later in [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]], Sith teachings discovered on Korriban and [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]] enticed the Jedi [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] and [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]] to the dark side, beginning the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]]. The Sith's alliance with the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]], a group of warrior-nomads descended from the [[Taung/Legends|Taungs]], in that war would prove to be the genesis of another threat to the Republic with the [[Mandalorian Wars]]. The Republic endured nearly fifty years of almost continuous fighting known as the [[Old Sith Wars]] as a result of Exar Kun until the [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]] was destroyed in [[3950 BBY]] by the redeemed Sith Lord [[Revan/Legends|Revan]].<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="NEC" />

[[File:New_Sith_Wars_map.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The galaxy during the final years of the [[Draggulch Period]].]]
By [[3700 BBY/Legends|3700 BBY]], the galaxy had been charted and settled as far as [[Farana/Legends|Farana]] in the north and Malastare in the south, but much of the northern and southern quadrants beyond the trade routes remained unsettled. At that time, however, the Brentaal-born explorer [[Freia Kallea/Legends|Freia Kallea]] extended the ancient [[Brentaal–Denon Route]] and linked several pre-exisiting praediums. By [[3693 BBY]], she had expanded the trade routes south of [[Denon/Legends|Denon]] as far as [[Imynusoph/Legends|Imynusoph]], mapping the full length of the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]], the only super-hyperroute to span the length of the galaxy. The ease with which vessels could now reach the northern and southern quadrants greatly expanded the Republic's footprint into the [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]] and the [[Western Reaches/Legends|Western Reaches]] and opened up countless new sources of minerals, crystals and gases.<ref name="TEA" /> From [[3681 BBY|3681]]-[[3642 BBY]], however, the Republic endured decades of [[Great Galactic War|war]] and [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|tension]] with a [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|resurgent Sith Empire]] formed by exiles from the Great Hyperspace War, led by the [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor Vitiate]]. A [[Galactic War|second Galactic War]] broke out between the two in 3642 BBY, and chaos reigned until the Sith Emperor's redoubt of the [[Eternal Empire]] was defeated.<ref name="SWTOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref><ref name="KOTFE">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Fallen Empire]]''</ref>

In the wars' aftermath, the galaxy enjoyed several centuries of relative prosperity, which ended in [[2000 BBY/Legends|2000 BBY]] with the dawn of the [[Draggulch Period]] and the start of the [[New Sith Wars]] when the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] Phanius proclaimed himself [[Darth Ruin/Legends|Darth Ruin]]. In the ensuing millennium of fighting between the Republic and the [[New Sith]], the Republic almost collapsed, culminating in the [[Republic Dark Age]] in the [[1100 BBY/Legends|final century]], when the Republic's authority effectively ceased to exist beyond the major trade routes and the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] communications network ceased to function. The New Sith Wars finally ended when the [[Army of Light/Legends|Army of Light]] led by the [[Jedi Lord]] [[Hoth (Jedi Lord)|Hoth]] defeated [[Skere Kaan]]'s [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] at the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan]]. A single Sith Lord, [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]], escaped to establish a [[Order of the Sith Lords|new Sith order]], while [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Tarsus Valorum/Legends|Tarsus Valorum]] proclaimed the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformations]], which rebuilt the Republic from the ground up.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="NEC" />

[[File:Reconquest_of_the_Rim.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The galaxy during the early years of the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]].]]
The Republic's final millennium was largely peaceful, but the provisions of the Ruusan Reformations led to an increase in lawlessness in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], which eventually found itself largely controlled by megacorporations or criminal cartels. This dissatisfaction was stoked into a [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist movement]] by the Sith, which had spent a millennium in hiding. Orchestrating the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Order of the Sith Lords]] managed to [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|destroy the Jedi Order]] and [[Declaration of a New Order|restore]] their Empire under [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]]. Sidious dissolved the Republic and replaced it with the short-lived [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and eventually [[Dissolution of the Imperial Senate/Legends|dissolved the Republic's trappings completely]]. A legacy of Imperial rule was the opening and widespread settlement of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]], as well as the charting and exploration of much of the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]. The Empire lasted for two decades of tyranny, but after the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] and the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|death]] of Darth Sidious at the hands of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], a [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] was [[Declaration of a New Republic/Legends|established]] from an [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|alliance]] of [[Alliance of Free Planets|free worlds]]. Despite this, the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|remnants]] of the Empire would continue to resist the new government for over a decade before finally signing a [[Pellaeon–Gavrisom Treaty|peace treaty]].<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="NEC" />

The [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] was a watershed moment in galactic history, marking the first time that the galaxy had been invaded by an [[Extragalactic/Legends|extra-galactic]] power, and the savagery of the war would influence galactic politics for over a century afterwards.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="NEC" /><ref name="Legacy">''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]''</ref> Not long after the conclusion of the Galactic Civil War, an [[Extragalactic/Legends|extra-galactic]] species known as the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] launched an invasion of the galaxy. The [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] devastated much of the galaxy, including [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], and cost the lives of some 365 trillion beings, though they were eventually [[Battle of Yuuzhan'tar|defeated]] by a new [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] of the Imperial Remnant, the remnants of the New Republic, and a host of the galaxy's lesser powers. Another outcome of the war was a normalisation of relations between the galaxy proper and the [[Chiss Ascendancy/Legends|Chiss Ascendancy]], the dominant power of the Unknown Regions. Within a few decades, stable hyperroutes and colonies had been established into the region and had removed much of its mystery.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="NEC" />

Some of the Yuuzhan Vong were incorporated in the [[galactic community]], but the post-Yuuzhan Vong War galaxy proved incredibly difficult to govern, resulting in a [[Second Galactic Civil War]] between the Galactic Alliance and a [[Confederation]] led by Corellia. Within a century, the Galactic Empire had been [[Fel Empire|restored]] under the [[Fel dynasty]], although this time without Sith backing. Ultimately, however, the [[Fel Empire]] was manipulated by the [[One Sith]], led by [[Darth Krayt]], to [[Sith–Imperial War|declare war]] upon the Galactic Alliance after the Sith exploited lingering hatred of the Yuuzhan Vong to to make it appear that they were planning to re-conquer the galaxy. The One Sith usurped the Imperial throne shortly afterwards, forming a [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|new Sith empire]], but the [[Second Imperial Civil War|resulting war]] between the Sith and the [[Galactic Alliance Remnant]] and the Fel-loyalist [[Empire-in-exile]] resulted in the [[Battle of Coruscant (Second Imperial Civil War)|Sith's defeat]]. Thereafter, the Galactic Alliance became the dominant government in the galaxy [[Galactic Federation Triumvirate|once again]].<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="NEC" /><ref name="Legacy" />

==Hyperspace==
[[File:Corellia_Antilles_Atlas.jpg|thumb|300px|[[Henrietya Antilles|Corellia Antilles]] views a [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] of the galaxy with its major trade routes highlighted.]]
Clear and stable paths through [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], known as [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] or hyperroutes, were the essential bedrock of galactic civilization. Hyperlanes provided safe trails for [[Starship/Legends|starships]] around the dangerous gravitic "[[Mass shadow/Legends|mass shadows]]" left in hyperspace by objects in [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]]. These routes were explored and established by [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] known as [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] [[Scout/Legends|explorers]] such as like [[Aitro Koornacht]] and [[Jori Daragon|Jori]] and [[Gav Daragon]]. Following are noteworthy routes that had shaped galactic history.<ref name="TEA" />

===The super-hyperroutes===
The [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|super-hyperroutes]] were the largest, longest and fastest hyperlanes in the galaxy, with several stretching from the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] all the way to the edge of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. The two oldest were the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]] and the [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]], both blazed after the development of the [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] in [[25,000 BBY/Legends|25,000 BBY]]. The Perlemian formed the northern border of [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] and linked the galactic capital of Coruscant to the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] training world of [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]] and the civilizations of the [[Tion Hegemony/Legends|Tion Hegemony]]. Early in the Republic's history, colonies and species along the breadth of the Perlemian appealed for Republic protection from the Tionese or the Hutts, fuelling the quick expansion of the young Republic. The Perlemian, known poetically as "the Axis", was dominated by [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]] early in the Republic's history, beginning the socio-economic divide that fuelled the [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|Alsakan Conflicts]].<ref name="EGW" /> The Perlemian emptied into Wild Space at the galaxy's fringe beyond [[Quermia/Legends|Quermia]].<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]] ensured the economic dominance of [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] within the emerging Republic and formed the southern border of the Slice. The portion of the Run Coreward of Corellia, known as "[[the Spin]]," was dominated by Coruscant early in the Republic's history, forming the divide with the Spin and Alsakan.<ref name="EGW" /> Rimward of Corellia, however, [[Corellian/Legends|Corellians]] and Humans of Corellian descent dominated and held substantial economic power in the sectors surrounding the Run for millennia afterwards. With the two eldest hyperroutes quickly established, it was much easier to explore in and around the Slice, causing a population boom that accounted for the galaxy's settlement patterns.<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Corellian Trade Spine/Legends|Corellian Trade Spine]] was established in [[5500 BBY/Legends|5500 BBY]], although the first led existed as far back as 25,000 BBY, linking Corellia and Duro. The Trade Spine intersected the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]] at [[Yag'Dhul/Legends|Yag'Dhul]] before extending Rimward to the [[Greater Javin/Legends|Greater Javin]] and past [[Terminus/Legends|Terminus]]. While offering rapid transit into the galactic southern quadrant, the Corellian Trade Spine never provided the same economic benefits as the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]]. Established around the same time, the Rimma was plotted by [[Givin/Legends|Givin]] hyperspatial cartographers and blazed by [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] scouts out of [[Herglic Space/Legends|Herglic Space]]. The Rimma helped usher in widespread colonization of the southern quadrant and enriched the worlds of the [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani sector]] in the Colonies. Significant planets on the Rimma included the rich industrialized world of [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]] on the junction with the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]], the [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] homeworld of [[Clak'dor VII/Legends|Clak'dor VII]], and the shipyards of [[Sluis Van/Legends|Sluis Van]].<ref name="TEA" />

The last super-hyperroute to be established, the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]], was the only one to span the entire length of the galaxy. Created almost entirely due to the efforts of the [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal]]-based scout [[Freia Kallea/Legends|Freia Kallea]], around [[3700 BBY/Legends|3700 BBY]] she extended the ancient [[Brentaal–Denon Route]] east, linking several obscure routes into a single passage that extended to the northern quadrant's galactic edge. She then pushed south of [[Denon/Legends|Denon]], blazing new routes to the Rim of the galaxy in the southern quadrant and opening great swaths of space to new colonization.<ref name="TEA" />

===Additional routes of interest===
The [[Metellos Trade Route/Legends|Metellos Trade Route]] was oriented west of Coruscant into [[the Negs]] as a failed attempt to discover a western analogue to the Perlemian Trade Route. Initially promising, its expansion stalled in the face of the hyperspace eddies close to the Unknown Regions, and explorers were able to extend its length only a few light-years each century until it eventually terminated in the [[Farlax sector/Legends|Farlax sector]]. A more successful Core Worlds hyperroute was the [[Koros Trunk Line/Legends|Koros Trunk Line]], an ancient pre-Republic route linking Coruscant to the [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] mines of the [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Koros system]]. Carbonite was essential to keeping the passengers of [[Sleeper ship/Legends|sleeper ships]] in [[Suspended animation/Legends|suspended animation]], and the route carried so much ore after the development of the hyperdrive that it became known as the Carbonite Pipeline.<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Salin Corridor/Legends|Salin Corridor]] was one of the oldest hyperlanes in the Outer Rim, first forged by [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot's]] [[Xim's empire|empire]] as the Warrior's Trace to support his [[Xim Wars|wars]] with the Hutts, and maintained by a "lighthouse network" of [[Hyperspace beacon/Legends|jump beacons]]. While many of the Xim-era beacons had long-since vanished, the stability of parts of the Salin Corridor was unusual and had intrigued hyperspace theorists for millennia. One of the longest routes in the Outer Rim, it began amid the Hutt-controlled Rim worlds near Aduba, meandered Coreward around the tip of Hutt Space, before turning north into the edges of the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]]. From there it skirted the [[Radama Void/Legends|Radama Void]], intersected the Hydian Way at [[Botajef/Legends|Botajef]], and emptied in the northern quadrant.<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Braxant Run/Legends|Braxant Run]] was the northern quadrant's most important route, beginning at [[Bandomeer/Legends|Bandomeer]] on the Hydian and twisting across the New Territories via [[Muunilinst/Legends|Muunilinst]] to [[Bastion/Legends|Bastion]]. The third of the Outer Rim's three most important routes, the [[Triellus Trade Route/Legends|Triellus Trade Route]] spanned more than 75,000 light-years from [[Centares/Legends|Centares]] to [[Enarc/Legends|Enarc]], forming one side of the "[[Spice Triangle/Legends|Spice Triangle]]." However, travel along the "Hutt Highway" was slow and often dangerous owing to smugglers, slavers and pirates operating out of Hutt Space.<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Ootmian Pabol/Legends|''Ootmian Pabol'']] connected the financial hubs of the Expansion Region with the heart of [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]]. A corruption of the [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]] ''Ootmian Pankapolla'', it was forged from [[Gyndine/Legends|Gyndine]] around [[12,000 BBY/Legends|12,000 BBY]] by Republic scouts to [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]]. Thriving trade turned Nal Hutta's moon [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] into a boomworld. However, the [[Supernova/Legends|supernova]] of the star of the [[Kyyr system]] in [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]] made the route unnavigable. The ''Ootmian'' was eventually restored, but the rise of the Corellian Run finished Nar Shaddaa as a respectable tradeworld, with legitimate business moving elsewhere and the moon becoming one of the galaxy's most notorious [[Shadowport/Legends|shadowports]]. It was speculated that the Kyyr supernova was thus responsible for the shift of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Kajidic/Legends|''kajidics'']] towards criminal enterprises.<ref name="TEA" />

There were some routes that were used for more illegal purposes, in particular the illicit trade of smuggling. One of the most infamous examples of illegal routes was the [[Kessel Run/Legends|Kessel Run]], an 18.5 [[Parsec/Legends|parsec]] three-stop route between Kessel and an area south of the [[Si'Klaata Cluster/Legends|Si'Klaata Cluster]] that was used during the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] by [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] who were smuggling [[Glitterstim/Legends|Glitterstim]] [[Spice/Legends|spice]] to the latter location without being caught by Imperial ships. Besides the two aforementioned locations, it also connected to the [[Kessel Trade Corridor]], the [[Triellus Trade Route/Legends|Triellus Trade Route]], and the [[Pabol Sleheyron/Legends|''Pabol Sleheyron'']] routes. The notorious smuggler Han Solo claimed to have navigated the Kessel Run in under 12 parsecs with his ship, the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], by skirting close to the [[Black hole/Legends|black holes]] that made up part of the Kessel Run.<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Ison Trade Corridor/Legends|Ison Corridor]] was a fairly small route within the Corellian Trade Spine, which had five system stops before reconnecting with the Spine, and was connected from the coreward region to the rimward region.<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Sisar Run/Legends|Sisar Run]] was a hyperspace trade route originating in the [[Tharin sector/Legends|Tharin sector]], where it passed through the heart of the Periphery, passing through Hutt Space and Srillur and bypassing the Si'Klatta Cluster before it splits at Sispe. It junctions with the [[Salin Corridor/Legends|Salin Corridor]], the [[Pabol Hutta/Legends|''Pabol Hutta'']], the ''Pabol Sleheyron'', and the [[Ac'fren Spur]] routes.<ref name="Sisar">''[[Secrets of the Sisar Run]]''</ref>

[[Myto's Arrow/Legends|Myto's Arrow]], named after its discoverer, the Galactic Republic scout [[Keos Myto]], was a route located in the Outer Rim that was used for travel between the [[Raioballo sector/Legends|Raioballo sector]] via [[Dantooine]] and the [[Obtrexta sector/Legends|Obtrexta sector]]. This route was connected with the [[Veragi Trade Route/Legends|Veragi Trade Route]] and the [[Braxant Run/Legends|Braxant Run]].<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Daragon Trail]], well known for being the longest blind jump to have been made successfully in the history of the galaxy, traveled between Korriban in the Outer Rim and Empress Teta (which at the time of the route's discovery was named Koros Major) in the Deep Core. It was named after Gav and Jori Daragon, the couple who discovered the route in [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]]. Portions of it were merged with the smuggling route [[Carbonite Run/Legends|Carbonite Run]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Government and politics==
===Senatorial representation===
Under the Galactic Republic, the peoples of the galaxy were represented in the [[Legislature|legislative body]] known as the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. Originally, any sufficiently-populated [[Star system/Legends|star system]] would return a [[Senator/Legends|senator]], but this was soon rejected as a recipe for gridlock as the Republic expanded massively and thousands of delegates attended Senate meetings. The Planetary Senate gave way to [[Sector/Legends|sectorial]] representation: the Republic was divided into sectors containing no more than fifty inhabited systems - it was feared that larger sectors would form the seeds of breakaway empires - which were each represented by a single sectorial senator. However, the price of passing this amendment was additional legislation that allowed many of the Republic's [[Core Founder/Legends|Core Founders]] to retain their planetary seats, giving extra votes to the most powerful Core and Colonies sectors.<ref name="TEA" />

To strict [[Galactic Constitution/Legends|Galactic Constitutionalists]], this was the Republic's "founding tyranny", a cynical scheme to preserve the power of the Core systems. Indeed, the awarding of single-system votes caused such an outcry that a compromise was reached: anyone recognized as a [[Junior Representative/Legends|representative]] of a single system had the right to petition the full Senate, a right still occasionally invoked under the [[New Republic Senate/Legends|New Republic Senate]].<ref name="TEA" />

Sectors grew to include thousands of star systems, but even with the "rule of fifty" widely ignored, the Republic expanded to include millions of sectors by [[17,000 BBY]], once again rendering the galaxy ungovernable. In the aftermath of the [[First Alsakan Conflict]], the [[Challat Compromise]] was adopted, which split the legislature into a seated Senate, whose members had full rights of address, and an unseated Senate, whose members had to petition for such rights. Predictably, the seated senators became power-brokers, and corruption thrived, with unseated senators having to trade the vast majority of their votes for the chance to be heard in the Senate.<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformations]] of [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]] saw a remarkable dismantling of central authority and reorganized the Republic into 1,024 regional sectors, each represented by a single senator, though once again a series of exceptions favored planets in the Core and Colonies. Additionally, the right of representation was extended to so-called [[Functional constituency|functional constituencies]] representing discreet cultural and species enclaves. While the galaxy was once again governable, the Reformations inevitably placed power into the hands of a very few, especially when the definition of functional constituencies was extended in [[124 BBY]] to the galaxy's mightiest guilds and corporations, chief among them the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]]. The Trade Federation bought up vast blocs of votes from poor sectors and gained control of key appointments in the bureaucracy, and by the time of the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]] was the Senate's greatest power and paralyzed the Senate in the face of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]].<ref name="TEA" />

[[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] stripped the Senate of most of its power during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and dissolved the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]] entirely in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]]. The [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] restored the body, but it inevitably again became mired in gridlock, archaic tradition, and corruption. When the New Republic was reorganized into the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]] during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the very name of the new state seemed to be an acceptance of the need for decentralization of power. However, efforts to rehabilitate the galaxy after the Yuuzhan Vong War depended heavily on centralized power, leading to the rebellion of independent-minded systems in a [[Confederation]] led by [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], and so the ancient problem of galactic democracy begun a [[Second Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="TEA" />

===Sectors===
[[File:ArkanisSector.jpg||thumb|left|150px|The [[Arkanis sector/Legends|Arkanis sector]], a post-Ruusan Reformations sector of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].]]
The basic political unit for much of galactic history was the [[Sector/Legends|sector]], largely artificial divisions of space organized for political, military and economic reasons. After the first years of the Galactic Republic, the star systems of the Republic were organized into sectors limited to fifty systems with substantial populations. As the Republic expanded, the huge number of sectors led to gridlock within the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], and some sectors swelled to include thousands of inhabited worlds, even as galactic civilization continued to expand wildly, until there were millions of sectors.<ref name="TEA" />

This was not resolved until the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformations]] of [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], which reorganized the galaxy into 1,024 regional sectors divided into constituent subsectors. The [[Chommell sector/Legends|Chommell sector]] of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]], for example, though fairly sparsely settled, contained some forty thousand inhabited worlds. Sectors by [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] included cultural groupings like the [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani sector]] and the [[Senex-Juvex/Legends|Senex-Juvex]], and business-controlled economic areas like the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]], but generally they were fairly arbitrary groupings of planets and colonies of very differing fates and cultures, such as the [[Gordian Reach/Legends|Gordian Reach]], the [[Arkanis sector/Legends|Arkanis sector]], and the [[Anoat sector/Legends|Anoat sector]].<ref name="TEA" />

The Ruusan Reformations created a number of problems with sectorial representation that would not be resolved until the Republic's end. A moratorium was included on the creation of new sectors, but settlers kept pushing beyond the Republic's frontier, reclaiming systems lost during the [[New Sith Wars]] and settling new worlds. Some of these systems were annexed by existing sectors, which caused some outlying sectors to swell to gargantuan proportions. Others became ''de facto'' corporate possessions, or were directly administered by the Republic bureaucracy and denied Senate representation, though it was claimed that they were "virtually represented" by other senators. The old Core sectors saw the rimward megasectors as a threat to their ancient power and prestige, while the directly-administered systems complained that their "virtual representation" was a farce. The reforms of [[124 BBY]] sought to address these issues, with many settled areas outside the Republic's borders becoming incorporated as [[Freestanding subsectors/Legends|freestanding subsectors]], with their representatives reporting to the senator of an associated sector.<ref name="TEA" />
