Until the final years of the Galactic Republic, sectors were governed by their [[Senator/Legends|senators]], while the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] had the right to appoint a [[Governor-General/Legends|Governor-General]] to coordinate military action within the sector during a state of emergency. [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] exploited this law frequently during the Clone Wars, culminating in the [[Sector Governance Decree/Legends|Sector Governance Decree]], that appointed a permanent new class of military governors to the regional sectors - the Galactic Empire's [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]].<ref name="TEA" /> The Galactic Empire also created or carved out a number of new sectors, overturning the Ruusan Reformations' moratorium, including the [[Indrexu sector/Legends|Indrexu sector]] in the [[Greater Tion]], and combined several freestanding subsectors to create the [[Baxel sector/Legends|Baxel]] and [[Zuma sector/Legends|Zuma sectors]].<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref>

[[File:GalaxyMap_JediArchives.png|thumb|right|250px|A map of the galaxy as seen in the [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi Archives]].]]

In the first years of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], any [[Planet/Legends|planet]] with a large enough population was granted a seat in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. However, even before the Galactic Republic had expanded beyond the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], this system of government was unworkable: the Senate's sheer size made debate interminable and consensus almost impossible to arrive to. The Planetary Senate was thus reorganized, with sectors being formed of groups of up to fifty star systems to act as the new constituencies, while recognized [[Junior Representative/Legends|representatives]] of a single planet or species still had the right to petition the full Senate. A prominent example of this towards the end of the Republic was [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]], representing the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] people of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="Ep2">{{Film|II}}</ref>

[[Planetary Governor/Legends|Planetary Governors]] represented the central government on a single [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. Their writ typically included the entire star system, though there were exceptions for systems that included multiple planets with huge populations or very different cultures, such as the [[Corellian system/Legends|Corellian system]]. In the eldest parts of the Core Worlds, systems and even individual planets were centers of political power, a relic of the Galactic Republic's origins. Elsewhere, systems were subservient in representation to subsectors, sectors and regions.<ref name="TEA" />

===Client states and Allied Regions===
[[File:Hutt_rgb_lg.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]] was a large stretch of the Outer and Mid Rims, dominated by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], that eluded central control for millennia.]]
The [[Allied Region]]s were independent states that freely joined the Galactic Republic as it expanded early in its history, with their rulers receiving the honorary title of [[Moff/Legends|Moff]]. By the time of the Clone Wars, most Allied Regions had been divided into sectors, but a handful endured as regions with a discreet cultural identity, such as the [[Trailing Sectors/Legends|Trailing Sectors]] or the [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]]; or a sector dominated by a single species, such as [[Trianii Space/Legends|Trianii Space]]. Several of these governments survived as [[Imperial client state|client states]] under the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and maintained a degree of independence, and were recognized by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] afterwards.<ref name="TEA" />

[[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]] referred to the large stretch of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Rimward]] [[The Slice/Legends|Slice]] controlled by the [[Grand Hutt Council/Legends|Hutt Ruling Council]], the governing body of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] species. Originally powerful warriors, the [[Hutt Empire]] [[Xim Wars|overthrew]] the [[Xim's empire|empire]] of [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot]], but a disastrous civil war around [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]] known as the [[Hutt Cataclysms]] forced a cultural reformation, beginning a new philosophy known as [[Kajidic/Legends|''kajidic'']], which stressed economic dominance over outright conquest. Hutt Space's borders ebbed and flowed over the millennia but the Hutts' power in both the economic and the criminal spheres endured, extending as far Coreward as [[Gyndine/Legends|Gyndine]] as the Galactic Republic decayed during the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]]. Hutt Space was nominally part of the Galactic Empire, but the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]] largely tolerated the Hutts' criminal dealings, as the Hutt Ruling Council was a known quantity as opposed to the possibility of hundreds of feuding Hutt crime lords. Hutt Space was devastated during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], but recovered surprisingly quickly, bringing with it a renewed Hutt militarism that was expressed when the region declared for the [[Confederation]] during the [[Second Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Corporate_sector.jpg||thumb|left|200px|The [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]], on the edge of the [[Tingel Arm/Legends|Tingel Arm]], was a business-dominated Imperial exclave.]]
The [[Corporate Sector Authority/Legends|Corporate Sector Authority]] (CSA) referred to the government of the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]], a region of close to thirty thousand star systems on the edge of the [[Tingel Arm/Legends|Tingel Arm]] ruled from [[Etti IV/Legends|Etti IV]], and was a collective of businesses and corporations granted exclusive rights to all resources in the territory. The experiment in corporate governance, while protecting the rights of workers, began after lessons were learned from the [[Outer Expansion Zone scandal]]. At the suggestion of [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Orman Tagge/Legends|Orman Tagge]], the Corporate Sector was vastly expanded under the Galactic Empire and it became an officially-sanctioned refuge for [[Loyalist/Legends|Loyalist]] corporations seeking to avoid [[Imperialization/Legends|nationalization]]. The CSA became the region's sole owner, employer, government, and military, while corporations that invested in the Authority would receive proportional shares of the profits.<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Centrality/Legends|Centrality]] was a long strip of territory to the north of Hutt Space, founded as a libertarian independent state in [[3350 BBY]]. [[Human/Legends|Human]]-dominated, the capital of [[Erilnar]] often fell under the influence of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Kajidic/Legends|''kajidics'']], which were often the beneficiaries of the profits of the Centrality's main export, the [[life-crystal]]s of [[Rafa V]]. The Centrality was formally an Imperial territory, but was generally left alone by [[Coruscant/Legends|Imperial Center]]. Emperor Palpatine's sole act concerning the region occurred several years prior to the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], when he gave ''de facto'' control of the Centrality to [[Rokur Gepta]], [[Sorcerers of Tund/Legends|Sorcerer of Tund]], who was later killed by [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] in defense of the region's native [[Oswaft]] at the [[Battle of ThonBoka]].<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Hapes Consortium/Legends|Hapes Consortium]] was the [[Monarchy/Legends|monarchical]] government of the [[Hapes Cluster/Legends|Hapes Cluster]], located in the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]]. Isolationist and matriarchal, the secretive [[Hapan]]s became legendary for their reputed wealth, beauty, pride, and aristocratic feuds. Emperor Palpatine's tolerance of the region's independence surprised many, and it was suggested that the Emperor maintained Hapes as a lesson to the galaxy in the dangers of insularity and decadence. The Hapes Consortium opened its borders after the [[Declaration of a New Republic/Legends|Declaration of a New Republic]].<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:HapesClusterMap-TEA.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The [[Hapes Cluster/Legends|Hapes Cluster]] was an isolationist grouping of 63 inhabited worlds ruled by the matriarchal [[Queen Mother]]s.]]
The [[Atrisian Commonwealth/Legends|Atrisian Commonwealth]] was a region of two hundred planets in the Core Worlds near the Unknown Regions. The political, diplomatic and military writings of [[Atrisia/Legends|Atrisia]], in particular the ''[[Sayings]]'' of [[Uueg Tching]], had been studied for millennia. The insular territory declared independence after Emperor Palpatine's death at [[Endor/Legends|Endor]] but later accepted Allied Region status in the New Republic. Similarly, [[Nouane (Allied Region)|Nouane]] began as a thriving Inner Rim empire beyond the Slice, and was renowned for its philosophers and thinkers, in particular the controversial [[Four Sages of Dwartii/Legends|Four Sages of Dwartii]]. Nouanese ministers were common in the young Republic, and the territory sought Allied Region status after being ravaged by the [[Mandalorian Crusaders]] in [[3963 BBY]]. The region of 212 planets was a loyal supporter of the Empire and declared independence under the New Republic.<ref name="TEA" />

[[Bothan Space/Legends|Bothan Space]] included some 150 settled systems in the Mid Rim, dominated by [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] colonists and ruled by the [[Combined Bothan Clans|Bothan Council]]. One of the few species close to Hutt Space to preserve their independence, the Bothans were credited with the diplomacy and espionage that preserved the stability of much of the Mid Rim. Bothan Space was one of the first regions to declare its support for the New Republic in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Botor Enclave/Legends|Botor Enclave]] and the [[Daupherm Planet States]] were two adjoining territories on the edge of the Core. The ursine [[Botori]] controlled two dozen star systems within a nebula while the Human [[Dawferim]] controlled just over thirty systems. The two states had fought no less than forty wars even after they accepted Allied Region status under the Galactic Republic, and both declared independence after the Declaration of a New Republic.<ref name="TEA" />

[[Herglic Space/Legends|Herglic Space]] referred to the shrunken remnant of the [[Herglic Trade Empire]]. It consisted of some forty star systems around the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]], but hundreds of worlds along the Rimma outside Herglic Space had substantial [[Herglic/Legends|Herglic]] populations. Herglic Space was brutally suppressed under the Empire but regained Allied Region status under the New Republic and the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]].<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Ktilac Regions/Legends|Ktilac Regions]] were a confederacy off the Perlemian Trade Route in the Inner Rim ruled by three species - the [[Ktilac]]s, the [[Murachaun]], and the [[Tocoyan]]s. Religiously fundamentalist, the region had evolved a common culture where each species was seen as complementary to the other two and the rest of the galaxy was seen as unholy. Each species ruled sixty-three star systems while another three were open to outlanders under strict conditions. The Regions maintained Allied Region status under the Galactic Alliance.<ref name="TEA" />

[[Paqwepori]] was a small cluster of ninety rich star systems just off the Corellian Run in the Mid Rim. [[Paqwepor Major]]'s bazaars were popular destinations for Republic traders expanding the Corellian Run for eons. The Paqwepori were known for their love of business and ambition while despising any law that could limit individual expression or initiative.<ref name="TEA" />

==Economy==
{{Main|Galactic economy}}
The spread of technology and civilization throughout the galaxy led to the development of the [[galactic economy]], the system of production, distribution, trade, and consumption of goods. Few planets were entirely self-sufficient, with some, such as the [[Factory world/Legends|factory worlds]] of [[Telti/Legends|Telti]] and [[Mechis III/Legends|Mechis III]], devoting their economies solely to the production of high-tech goods but relying on [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworlds]] for food. In turn, these agriworlds relied on on manufacturing worlds to supply heavy equipment to harvest and process [[Foodstuff/Legends|foodstuffs]], and chemical industries to produce fertilizers and pesticides.<ref name="EGTWAT">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>

The importance of the galactic economy meant that a number of megacorporations were able to acquire immense economic and political power. In the years prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], a conglomerate of shipping and merchant cartels, controlled the votes of hundreds of star systems in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] by making their commerce dependent on its [[Trade Federation Merchant Fleet|Merchant Fleet]] and enforcing deals with the [[Trade Defense Force]].<ref name="EGW" /> Companies such as the [[SoroSuub Corporation/Legends|SoroSuub Corporation]], which under the Empire outright controlled the government of the planet [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]], produced goods for hundreds of fields. [[Tagge Corporation|TaggeCo]] controlled hundreds of star systems and dozens of subsidiaries, making it one of the galaxy's most influential organizations. Even relatively small businesses, such as the [[Figg conglomerate]] in the [[Greater Javin/Legends|Greater Javin]], commanded substantial influence on their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworlds]] and sectors.<ref name="EGTWAT" />

The main currency of the Galactic Republic was the [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|Galactic Credit Standard]], divided into ten [[Decicred/Legends|decicreds]].<ref name="SOTE">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref>

==Demographics==
===Population===
[[File:GalacticPopulation.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Galactic Population map]]
Of the galaxy's one billion settled systems, the majority of these were lightly-settled colonies of little note that were often not even marked on [[Sector/Legends|sector]] maps.<ref name="TEA" /> The [[Chommell sector/Legends|Chommell sector]], for instance, contained thirty-six worlds that were sufficiently populated to merit representation in the Galactic Republic, but also contained 40,000 settled dependencies, in addition to 300,000,000 barren, unsettled [[Star/Legends|stars]].<ref name="AOTC:ICS">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref>

During the days of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] more than 69 million [[Star system/Legends|systems]] met the requirements for Imperial representation, and 1.75 million planets were considered full member worlds. The population of the nearly 70 million systems that the Empire was responsible for amounted to more than 100 quadrillion beings.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="AtlasEndnotes" /><ref name="RPG">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'', Second Edition]]</ref>

===Races and species===
{{Main|Species/Legends}}
Because only around a quarter of the galaxy's four hundred billion stars had been thoroughly surveyed, scientists were uncertain as to the true number of intelligent species. The Galactic Empire recognized five million intelligent species, though it was mathematically accepted that galactic civilization had yet to discover a large number of species and the total could be as high as twenty million.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="AtlasEndnotes" />

[[File:Ithorian-Human-Baragwin.jpg|thumb|left|200px|An [[Ithorian/Legends|Ithorian]] playing holochess against a [[Unidentified Human scoundrel|Human]] opponent, as a [[Baragwin/Legends|Baragwin]] observes.]]
In classical history, the dominant species were [[Human/Legends|Humans]]. Originating from the Core Worlds, Humans were the most populous species in the galaxy and so tended to form the basis of the major [[:Category:Governments|governments]]. Sentients other than Humans were sometimes known as "[[Alien/Legends|aliens]]," though the term "non-Human" was considered less offensive. Nevertheless, the [[Humanocentrism|Humanocentric]] definition of races was considered unacceptable by some, and simply another expression of unwarranted Human dominance.<ref name="X-Wing: The Krytos Trap">''[[X-Wing: The Krytos Trap]]''</ref> Other notable spacefaring species included the [[Baragwin/Legends|Baragwin]], who had long since forgotten their homeworld and roamed the galaxy as merchants; the [[Duros/Legends|Duros]], a founding species of the Republic and creators of the modern hyperdrive; the [[Herglic/Legends|Herglics]] of [[Giju/Legends|Giju]], the founders of the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]]; the [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] of [[Kinyen/Legends|Kinyen]], who had settled countless colonies, including [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]]; and the [[Ithorian/Legends|Ithorians]], who had long maintained great networks of [[Ithorian Herdship|Herdships]] for galactic trade, and transferred their civilization there after [[Ithor/Legends|Ithor]] was devastated during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].<ref name="TEA" />

Although not considered a race for obvious reasons, [[Droid/Legends|droids]] formed a significant part of society, helping and coexisting with the population. On [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], higher level droids were considered equal as fellow sentients.

===Extragalactic interaction===
{{Main|Extra-galactic}}
[[File:BrodoAsogiSenate.png|thumb|right|200px|Whether the [[Asogian/Legends|Asogian]] expedition to another galaxy succeeded or not is unknown.]]
Extra-galactic travel was difficult due to a [[circumferential hyperspace barrier]] that prevented hyperspace routes very far outside the disk, and beyond this, the barren vastness of the [[Intergalactic Void]]. However, by the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], contact had been established with the two small galaxies orbiting the galaxy: the [[Rishi Maze/Legends|Rishi Maze]], also known as Companion Aurek, and [[Firefist]], also known as Companion Besh. The [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]] had influence as far as these locations.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref>

The [[Extragalactic Society]] was an organization devoted to the search for life outside the galaxy. Two major expeditions were launched around the period of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in an effort to explore beyond the galaxy: the [[Outbound Flight Project]] was intended to settle another galaxy but was destroyed by the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] after it accidentally entered their territory in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]].<ref name="OF">[[Outbound Flight (novel)|''Outbound Flight'']]</ref> In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], during the last days of the Republic, the [[Brodo Asogi]] leader [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Grebleips/Legends|Grebleips]] sent an expedition to another galaxy, but all information about the outcome of this endeavor remained unknown.<ref name="Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:241">{{InsiderCite|84|Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:241}}</ref>

[[File:YuuzhanVong_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The [[Yuuzhan Vong]] were the most infamous extra-galactic species.]]
Just after the Battle of Endor, the [[Nagai/Legends|Nagai]] and the [[Tof/Legends|Tofs]], races native to the companion galaxy of Firefist, invaded the galaxy, the Nagai hoping to escape the Tofs, who had oppressed them for centuries. Assisted by the [[Alliance of Free Planets]] and the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]], the Nagai defeated the Tofs and returned to liberate their home galaxy, bringing the [[Nagai–Tof War]] to a close.<ref name="EGW" />

Among the best known extra-galactic aliens were those that had fled from the [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy]]: the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] races of the [[Abominor]] and the [[Silentium]], and the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] themselves and their slave soldiers, the [[Chazrach]]. The Abominor and the Silentium fought a [[Silentium–Abominor War|devastating war]] before the Yuuzhan Vong rose up against both and drive them from their galaxy. Of those Silentium and Abominor that survived, two, the [[Great Heep]] and [[Vuffi Raa]], established themselves in the galaxy proper around the time of the Galactic Civil War. The former was destroyed on [[Biitu]] and the latter was recovered by the Silentium after the [[Battle of ThonBoka]].<ref name="Droids">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

After driving the Silentium and the Abominor from their galaxy, the Yuuzhan Vong turned inward and fought their own civil war, the [[Cremlevian War]], which stripped much of their galaxy of life. Seeking a new home, the Yuuzhan Vong and the Chazrach crossed the [[Intergalactic Void]] for millennia until they arrived in the galaxy, beginning a [[True Way|religious]] [[Yuuzhan Vong War|war]] which almost destroyed galactic civilization while it was just recovering from the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="Star Wars: The New Jedi Order">''[[Star Wars: The New Jedi Order]]''</ref>

==Speech==
{{Main|Language/Legends}}
The ''lingua franca'' of the galaxy was [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]], which had its origins as a Human language of Coruscant known as [[Old Galactic Standard]]. As the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] expanded, Old Galactic Standard took influences from [[Durese/Legends|Durese]], [[Bothese]], and [[Olys Corellisi/Legends|Olys Corellisi]], becoming [[Mid-Galactic Standard]] by [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]].<ref name="Gamer 2">{{GamerCite|2|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Duros}}</ref><ref name="XWD3">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/ximweek04/index.html|text=Xim Week: ''The Despotica'' (Part III: Xim at Vondor)|int=Xim Week: The Despotica}}</ref> Influence from the [[Dromnyr]] language after the [[Vultan]]s joined the Galactic Republic around [[14,000 BBY]] saw the evolution of Mid-Galactic Standard into the modern Basic.<ref name="POTJS" /> Humans being the dominant species of the galaxy, Basic was adopted by many non-Human species as well.

The second most common language was [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]], expanded through the criminal and financial activity of the Hutts, and so it was adopted throughout the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] by other species that were in close cooperation with them throughout the ages, such as the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodians]] and the [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarians]].<ref name="GPBTG">[[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'']]</ref>

The dominant [[Writing/Legends|writing system]] in the galaxy was [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]], derived from the script of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] by its former subject species after the Empire collapsed, though the symbols themselves were possibly much older.<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm 3">[[Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm 3|''Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm'' 3]]</ref><ref name="Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 1">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 1|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 1]]</ref> Aurebesh spread throughout the galaxy during the [[Tionese War]] between the young Galactic Republic and the [[Honorable Union of Desevro and Tion|Honorable Union of Desevro & Tion]], when the new [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]] found it needed to standardize its communications, and so adopted the writing system of Coruscant. The second most-common writing system was the [[High Galactic/Legends|High Galactic alphabet]], promoted by [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]] after [[17,000 BBY]] during the [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|Alsakan Conflicts]] as part of its efforts to be recognized as the galactic capital. Derived from [[Tionese/Legends|Tionese characters]], the High Galactic alphabet was popular among the upper class, and as late as [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], one-third of Republic citizens who spoke Basic used the High Galactic alphabet. Consequently, notices were often written in both Aurebesh and High Galactic.<ref name="WW">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/writtenword/index.html?page=1|text=The Written Word|int=The Written Word}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
===Name===
No serious attempt has been made to give the galaxy an official astronomical name. It is generally referred to by the out-of-universe descriptive phrase "the ''Star Wars'' galaxy". According to ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', the [[Nagai/Legends|Nagai]] of [[Firefist]] refer to the main galaxy as ''Skyriver'', which is the closest any official material has come to giving the galaxy an in-universe name. We don't know, however, whether or how members of the [[galactic community]] refer to their own home galaxy (the way we call ours the "[[Wikipedia:Milky Way|Milky Way]]").

"The Galaxy Far, Far Away", often abbreviated GFFA is the unofficial name given by many fans to the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] that is the setting for the ''[[Star Wars]]'' films and their spin-offs. This galaxy in the films is referred to simply as "the galaxy." It springs from the introduction present at the beginning of each of the films, many of the video games, and even some fan films and novels:
:''A long time ago in a galaxy far,''
:''far away....''
Eventually the use of the acronym GFFA became so prevalent that [[Del Rey]] named the post-[[Star Wars: The New Jedi Order|New Jedi Order]] government, the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]], in honor of the term.<ref name="sue">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=93010&start=9593&tstart=0#3076125|thread=Welcome some BCaT VIPs|user=[[Sue Rostoni]]|date=2002-11-18|time=1:32 PM}}</ref>

===Relation to Earth===
The opening words of each ''Star Wars'' film place the galaxy in the same plane of existence as ours, as they declare it to be a finite distance&mdash;"far, far away"&mdash;from us, but nothing more of its location has been revealed. Humans exist in both galaxies, and Galactic Basic is essentially the same as modern-day [[Wikipedia:English language|English]], including (but not limited to) its [[Wikipedia:British English|British]], [[Wikipedia:American English|American]], [[Wikipedia:New Zealand English|New Zealander]], [[Wikipedia:Caribbean English|Caribbean]], and [[Wikipedia:Indian English|Indian]] variants. Additionally, many cultural traditions (from the [[handshake]] to [[Marriage/Legends|marriage]]) are similar or identical in both galaxies, but these similarities remain unexplained.

Similarly, the time frame the galaxy and the events occurring in it occurred in compared to that of Earth is not made clear other than the opening words declaring that they took place "A long time ago." The teaser trailer for ''A New Hope'' opened with the line "Somewhere in space, this may all be happening right now..." It should be noted that, originally, when George Lucas was writing the first film in its [[The Star Wars story synopsis|initial treatment]], he had intended for the galaxy to not only occur within the same galaxy as our own, but the time frame would have been specifically cited as occurring within the thirty-third century.<ref name="How Star Wars Conquered the Universe">{{BookCite|author=Chris Taylor|title=How Star Wars Conquered the Universe: The Past, Present Future of a Multibillion Dollar Franchise|publisher=Basic Books|date=2014}} "The third mode that [George] Lucas intended to use to depict [American involvement in the] Vietnam [War]&mdash;the allegorical, futuristic lens&mdash;was only just taking shape, but already it was being influenced by Lucas' thinking about the present tense.*Lucas was fascinated by the notion of how a tiny nation could overcome the largest military power on Earth, and this was baked into The Star Wars right from its earliest notes in 1973: "A large technological empire going after a small group of freedom fighters."<br />*Though Star Wars was ultimately set "a long time ago," Lucas's earliest plan was to set it in the thirty-third century.</ref><ref name="The Star Wars: Story Synopsis">[[The Star Wars story synopsis|''The Star Wars'' story synopsis]]</ref> [[Walter Murch]], an associate of Lucas' since his days working at American Zoetrope, implied that part of the reason for the decision to change the setting to occurring in a galaxy "far, far away" from our own was so Lucas could both make the movie and at the same time get away with pushing anti-[[Wikipedia:Vietnam War|Vietnam War]] messaging in the film as a transubstantiated remake of [[Wikipedia:Apocalypse Now|''Apocalypse Now'']], as he could not get the message out directly due to the events of Vietnam still occurring at the time Lucas started making ''Star Wars''.<ref name="The Conversations">{{BookCite|author=Michael Ondaatje|title=The Conversations: Walter Murch and the Art of Editing Film|date=2004}} "Originally George Lucas was going to direct ('Apocalypse Now'), so it was a project that George and John [Milius] developed for [American] Zoetrope. That was back in 1969. Then when Warner Brothers cancelled the funding for Zoetrope, the project was abandoned for a while. After the success of 'American Graffiti' in 1973, George wanted to revive it, but it was still too hot a topic, the [Vietnam] war was still on, and nobody wanted to finance something like that. So George considered his options: What did he really want to say in 'Apocalypse Now?' The message boiled down to the ability of a small group of people to defeat a gigantic power simply by the force of their convictions. And he decided, All right, if it's politically too hot as a contemporary subject, I'll put the essence of the story in outer space and make it happen in a galaxy long ago and far away. The rebel group were the North Vietnamese, and the Empire was the United States. And if you have 'the force,' no matter how small you are, you can defeat the overwhelmingly big power. 'Star Wars' is George's transubstantiated version of 'Apocalypse Now.'"</ref><ref name="YOMYOMF">{{WebCite|url=http://www.yomyomf.com/star-wars-is-a-metaphor-for-the-vietcong-kicking-american-ass-in-the-vietnam-war|text='Star Wars' is a Metaphor for the Vietcong Kicking American Ass in the Vietnam War?|date=2015-12-16|archivedate=20160610224959}}</ref> George Lucas in ''[[The Making of Star Wars]]'' gave a similar reason for the change.<ref name="Making of Star Wars">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]'' "A lot of my [George Lucas's] interest in Apocalypse Now was carried over into ''Star Wars'', I figured that I couldn't make that film because it was about the Vietnam War, so I would essentially deal with some of the same interesting concepts that I was going to use and convert them into space fantasy, so you'd have essentially a large technological empire going after a small group of freedom fighters or human beings."</ref>

===The ''Empire Strikes Back'' debate===
[[File:Empire_endshot.png|thumb|left|200px|The controversial scene from ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]
At the end of [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']], characters aboard the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Rebel fleet]] see a celestial object from some distance away. Some fans have said that it rotates too fast to be a galaxy and at that distance a galaxy would not emit as much light as is portrayed in the film.

Some sources have said that the fleet spent some time hiding outside the galactic disk, probably intending to refer to this scene.<ref name="TEA" /> According to the [[1996]] ''[[Tales of the Bounty Hunters]]'' story ''[[Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM]]'', the object in the film ''is'' the galaxy, and the Rebel fleet had journeyed to a [[Haven (rendezvous point)|point]] in space far removed from the galactic plane.<ref name="Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM">{{StoryCite|story=Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref> This point was not outside of the galactic plane, per se, but rather above the galactic plane.

Since the release of ''Tales of the Bounty Hunters'', the object has been inconsistently identified. ''[[The Complete Star Wars Trilogy Scrapbook]]'', first released in [[1997]], identifies the object as a spinning star formation. In [[2002]], the [[StarWars.com#DVD-ROM Exclusive Content|''Episode II'' DVD-ROM Exclusive Content]] stated that the bright object may be the [[Star cluster/Legends|cluster]] known as the [[Rishi Maze/Legends|Rishi Maze]]. In [[2003]], [[Leland Chee]] confirmed on the [[StarWars.com]] [[Starwars.com Message Boards|Message Boards]] that the object was indeed the ''Star Wars'' galaxy,<ref>{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=118855&start=281#4612881|thread=Galaxy Map Discussion|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2003-08-18|time=8:59 AM}}</ref> which was reinforced by the release of ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' in [[2009]], which established that the Rebel fleet regrouped at a point above the galactic plane.<ref name="TEA" />

===History of published maps===
Several publications have contained "maps" of the galaxy, although they are at best two-dimensional [[Wikipedia:Graphical projection|projections]] of a three-dimensional galaxy. The first maps of the ''Star Wars'' galaxy were published in [[roleplaying game]] sourcebooks by [[West End Games]], and contained detail maps of regions and sectors. The [[Elrood sector/Legends|Elrood sector]] was mapped in ''[[Planets of the Galaxy, Volume Three]]'', the [[Brak sector/Legends|Brak sector]] in ''[[Flashpoint! Brak Sector]]'', the [[Kathol sector/Legends|Kathol sector]] in ''[[The DarkStryder Campaign]]'', and the [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani sector]] and the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]] in ''[[Lords of the Expanse]]''.<ref name="Charting">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-maps-charting-the-galaxy|text=''Star Wars'' Maps: Charting the Galaxy|nolive=1}}</ref>

Despite these partial maps, it would not be until [[1998]], with the release of the CD-ROM digital encyclopedia ''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'' that the first full, official galactic map was released. This map placed the most important planets from the films and the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]]. The map provided a top-down view of the ''Star Wars'' galaxy, with concentric rings indicating the various regions from the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], as well as placing [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], which would feature in the upcoming [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="Charting" />

[[1999]] saw the release of [[Star Wars: The New Jedi Order|''The New Jedi Order'']] series, which included a detailed galactic map in each novel that tracked the course of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War|Yuuzhan Vong invasion]]. The maps in these books showed an isometric projection of the galaxy, and included the spiral arms and empty galactic west known as the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]. Each novel included the same basic map, which mapped planets from the existing lore as well as newly visited worlds of the ''New Jedi Order'' stories. [[2000]]'s [[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']] used the same map in its endpapers.<ref name="Charting" />

''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]'', also released in 2000, returned to a map using concentric circles, similar to the ''Behind the Magic'' map, but with broadly similar planet placements to ''The New Jedi Order'' map. Other maps, however, beginning with [[Star Wars Gamer 5|''Star Wars Gamer'' 5]], elaborated on the concept of ''The New Jedi Order'' map, and increasingly-detailed color maps were published in some issues of ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]'' ([[The Official Star Wars Fact File 1|1]], [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 56|56]], [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 139|139]]). A large poster map was provided in [[2003]]'s [[Star Wars Insider 65|''Star Wars Insider'' 65]], and ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' of [[2005]] also had a spread with an updated galaxy map and its most notable systems, and was the first to mark the locations of the planets of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']].<ref name="Charting" />

2009 saw the release of ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', which did away with isometric projections in favor of a top-down chart, while keeping regional borders and planet placements largely the same. As well as a large galaxy map, ''The Essential Atlas'' also included numerous historical, regional, and sectoral maps and developed a coordinate system and galactic compass. In addition, ''The Essential Atlas'' included an index of 4,387 [[Star system/Legends|star systems]], assigning each a coordinate, sector and region. ''The Essential Atlas'' has since been expanded with an [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|Online Companion]], which includes an updated index placing 5,085 star systems, believed to be every system mentioned in ''[[Star Wars Legends]]'', as well as maps of the sectors of the Outer Rim, Mid Rim, and Expansion Region.<ref name="Charting" />

===Video game maps===
The chapter selection of [[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']] ([[1995]]) was the first appearance of what can be considered a galaxy map, consisting of a generic galactic shape on which the supposed location of the current mission is highlighted; the highlights, however, do not correspond to canonical coordinates of said locations (e.g. selecting the [[Greater Javin/Legends|Greater Javin]] campaign wrongly highlights the Galactic Core). The [[1998]] video game [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] would provide an interface of a galaxy map divided up into 20 sectors and 200 systems; however, these positions are provided only as a game mechanic and have been contradicted by later official sources.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://starwarsatlas.uw.hu/rebellion2.htm|text=List of ''Rebellion'' sectors and planets and their correctness|author=Modi|archivedate=20200105150512}}</ref>
